key_insight: TATVA frames quantum circuit synthesis as a sequential reinforcement-learning problem, using DQN and PPO to build compact high-fidelity circuits gate by gate.
engineering_relevance: It offers an automated path to prepare quantum states with fewer hand-designed rules, which is useful for scalable quantum algorithm compilation and near-term hardware workflows.
method: Two RL agents (DQN and PPO) propose gates one step at a time.
After each gate, fidelity is evaluated and the best action is selected.
A post-hoc optimization step reduces circuit depth while preserving fidelity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports synthesis up to 5 qubits, achieving fidelity as high as 0.999999 and testing generalization on target states not seen during training.
watch_item: Results may depend on simulator fidelity and the approach could be harder to scale as qubit count and action space grow.
paper_title: TATVA: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Quantum Circuit Synthesis
